_comment: Hand-curated strongman + grip world records - the source layer tools/build_records.py merges into the bundled dataset. Neither sport has an open database or API, so every entry here was verified by hand against the cited source (headline records against two or more independent sources) on the as_of date. Editorial rules: current records only (superseded or equipment-nullified marks stay out); entries that could not be verified against a live source are dropped, not guessed; scope is 'official' when the sanctioning body in 'fed' recognizes the mark, 'unofficial' for well-documented marks outside a sanctioning body's list; confidence is 'high' (2+ independent sources) or 'medium' (single primary source, or a detail like the exact date unsettled). Known exclusions: strongman yoke/farmer's carries (no standardized weight-distance pairing exists across events), the u105 strongman deadlift (records archive unreachable, could not verify), Saxon bar (bar specs fragment across federations - numbers are not comparable), and the Inch Dumbbell (fixed-weight implement, no ratified variable-weight record).

records.lift_display: Vertical Bar Deadlift - 1 bar, 2", one hand (right hand, all-time best across bodyweight classes)
records.notes: 260 lb (117.93 kg), 2013 Grip Championships. Extracted as the single highest value across all USAWA bodyweight classes (35 through 125+) for the RIGHT-hand version of this lift, from the current official USAWA record book (Individual Record List, dated 2026-07-02). USAWA also tracks a LEFT-hand version separately; current left-hand best is Ben Edwards, 242 lb (109.77 kg), BW95, 2012-07-15. Spec: 1 bar, 2" diameter, max 18" length, one hand, per usawa.com/vertical-bar-deadlift-1-bar-2-1-hand/. Older secondary sources (blog posts) cite Edwards at 235 lb or 251 lb as 'the' record — those predate the current book and are superseded by Goetsch's 260 lb mark. USAWA bodyweight class of the holder: 95kg.

records.notes: 137 lb (62.14 kg), 2015 Club Championships. Extracted as the single highest value across all USAWA female bodyweight classes for the RIGHT-hand version, from the current official USAWA record book dated 2026-07-02. 9 lb (4.08 kg), Frank's Record Breaker meet. Weaver Stick: 36in stick w/ 5.5in handle, cord attached 42in from handle end per USAWA rules (usawa.com/the-weaver-stick/); lifted with straight locked elbow, arm not touching body. Weight classes are USAWA's kg bodyweight bands (35...125+), open/all-age ('ALL') category value shown. USAWA bodyweight class of the holder: 125+kg.

3.75 lb (1.70 kg), Light Weight Decathlon Challenge RD, Columbia, MO. USAWA bodyweight class of the holder: 105kg.

Value = IronMind's official 'c. 322.5 lb' (146.28 kg) nominal closing-force rating for the No. 3.5 gripper (bridge between No.3 and No.4), per https://ironmind.com/product-info/ironmind-grippers/captains-of-crush-grippers/. 21 people certified since 2008; first: 'Tex' Henderson (USA), 2008-08-05. Most recent batch (2021): Tanner Merkle (USA), Ivan Cuk (USA), Nikita Yurkovets (Belarus). No female certifications recorded to date. Full roster verified by direct fetch of the who's-who page (count corrects an AI web-search summary that miscounted 28).
51.40 kg (113.31 lb). Block + 15in Olympic loading pin + carabiner = 3.4kg/7.5lb included in total. Thumbless grip not permitted; 1 min to complete lift.

Original spec 330 lb/150 kg. Startingstrongman.com's own records page (archived Dec 2025) still lists this as the current men's Open World Record. Wikipedia's own article separately annotates the same 150kg/2018 mark as a 'former world record' but no higher verified successor could be found anywhere in searches (Savatinov's 141-143kg marks, cited elsewhere as a 'world record,' are all lower and are apparently national/promotion-specific, not the open WR). Treat the 'former' label with caution -- may be a stale Wikipedia annotation.

Original spec 183.4 lb. Daily Hive (independent sports outlet) reports this lift 'surpassed the open record of 180 pounds' at the time. CONTESTED: startingstrongman.com's own circus-dumbbell records page (archived Dec 2025) still lists the women's Open record as Kristin Rhodes, 79.5 kg/175 lb (2019) -- i.e. lower than and apparently unaware of Belliveau's 2022 lift. This is a known gap in strongwoman record-keeping (no single unified sanctioning body); flagging as unofficial/contested rather than dropping since two independent outlets did report it as a record at the time.

Original spec 225 lb/102 kg. Single-publisher sourcing (startingstrongman.com), though it is still listed as current on the most recent (May 2026) archived snapshot of their dedicated log-press records page. A 2022 YouTube/Facebook post credits Kate Connolly (GB) with a '101kg/222lb U64 Log Press World Record' -- that is LESS than Falcone's 102kg, so it cannot be a supersession as titled; likely a British national record or promoter mislabel. Did not find a verified figure higher than Falcone's 102kg, so kept Falcone as current.
Original spec 622.8 lb (622-623 lb reported, minor rounding across outlets). Lovelace weighed in at 62.5 kg. Superseded her own earlier 272.5kg (2020) mark.

Original spec 222.6-222.7 lb. Held at Kaos Strength Gym, Preston, England. Superseded her own earlier 92.5kg (Jan 2020) mark. Later broken by Faye Pittman's 105kg u73 mark (different weight class, see separate entry).

Original spec 576.5 lb. Reported as 4.1x her bodyweight (~63.8kg). Distinct implement/event from the standard-bar deadlift above. Also reported as a simultaneous heavyweight/absolute axle-deadlift WR at the time. Superseded her own earlier 233.5kg/515lb (May 2022, Clash of the 64's) mark. A later 320kg/705lb pull (Apr 2023) was an Instagram training lift, NOT a sanctioned competition attempt -- excluded per rules.
